chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'And the chaste women from those who were given the Scripture before you.'
And the chaste women from those who were given the Scripture before you.
He said: 'It is abrogated by His saying: 'And do not hold onto the ties of marriage of the disbelieving women.''
And do not hold onto the ties of marriage of the disbelieving women.

key_terms.أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir, peace be upon him)
key_terms.مَنْسُوخَةٌ: Abrogated (a ruling superseded by a later one)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying women of the Book according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Zurarah queries Imam al-Baqir regarding the permissibility of marrying chaste women of the People of the Book, to which the Imam responds that the ruling is abrogated (mansukh) by the command not to retain the bonds of disbelieving women. This narration highlights the Shia scholarly view that the initial permission was temporary, ultimately leading to the prohibition of maintaining such marriages, a position distinct from some Sunni interpretations that view the verse as abrogating the prohibition rather than the permission.
